title: Triage rubric and intake form for Reserved Throughput & SLA Profiles
creator: Avery Kline
description:
Purpose: Create a repeatable, low-friction intake and triage rubric for enterprise requests that need reserved throughput, SLA targets, and guidance on GPU class and autoscaling policies. Scope: public-facing intake form, internal triage rubric that maps customer requirements to profiles (e.g., bronze/silver/gold), recommended GPU classes, and prescriptive scaling policies. Out of scope: billing/legal contract language and final SLA sign-off.
Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form captures required signals to recommend an initial profile (target p95 latency, sustained RPS, burst windows, dataset size, model family, security requirements).
- Triage rubric translates signals to a recommended profile and GPU class with clear trade-offs (cost, latency, availability).
- Internal playbook for edge cases (multi-region, on-prem, private cloud) and escalation path to solutions engineering.
- A sample customer-facing one-pager and template email for sales to set expectations.
Proposed profiles:
- Bronze: 1-2x reserved GPUs, best-effort latency SLO, cost-optimized (quantization auto-enabled).
- Silver: sustained throughput SLA, defined burst policy, KV cache enabled, 2x reserved GPUs.
- Gold: high-availability SLA with cross-region fallback, dedicated capacity with warm pools and guaranteed burst capacity.
Decision notes: Prefer prescriptive profiles vs completely custom proposals to speed onboarding. Where customers need custom SLAs, route to enterprise onboarding and legal. Metrics to use: sustained tokens/sec, p95 latency under typical prompt mix, failure rate under 95th throughput.
Rollout plan: alpha with Solutions Eng and 3 pilot customers (2 startups, 1 enterprise) -> incorporate feedback -> beta for sales org -> GA into onboarding playbook.
